title: Extracting Common ADSL Variables Across Domains
text: clinical data analysis, ADSL (Subject-Level Analysis Dataset) often contains critical variables reused across various analysis domains (e.g., ADAE, ADLB, ADLBC). extract_common_adsl_variables() function adrgOS package helps identify summarize common variables, providing insights variable provenance consistency across domains.

title: Extracting Common ADSL Variables Across Domains
text: can install adrgOS GitHub:

title: Extracting Common ADSL Variables Across Domains
text: First, extract variable metadata Define-XML file using extract_variable_info_from_define(). Define-XML file package (inst/define.xml), can locate system.file().
code: library(adrgOS) define_path <- system.file("define.xml", package = "adrgOS") if (file.exists(define_path)) {   variable_info <- extract_variable_info_from_define(define_path) } else {   stop("Define-XML file not found in the package.") }

title: Extracting Common ADSL Variables Across Domains
text: Use extract_common_adsl_variables() identify variables present ADSL domains.
code: common_vars <- extract_common_adsl_variables(   variable_info_df = variable_info,   adsl_dataset_name = "ADSL",      # Name of the ADSL dataset   include_sas_info    = TRUE,        # Include SAS field and length info   min_domains_count   = 1,           # Minimum number of domains   sort_by             = "domains_count"  # Sort by number of domains )  # View the first few rows head(common_vars) #>   Variable SASFieldName DataType Length            Description  Origin #> 1      AGE          AGE  integer      8                    Age Derived #> 2   AGEGR1       AGEGR1     text      5     Pooled Age Group 1 Derived #> 3  AGEGR1N      AGEGR1N  integer      8 Pooled Age Group 1 (N) Derived #> 4     RACE         RACE     text     32                   Race Derived #> 5    RACEN        RACEN  integer      8               Race (N) Derived #> 6      SEX          SEX     text      1                    Sex Derived #>   CodelistOID DomainsCount               DomainsFound  SASLength #> 1                        4 ADADAS, ADAE, ADLBC, ADTTE integer(8) #> 2                        4 ADADAS, ADAE, ADLBC, ADTTE    text(5) #> 3                        4 ADADAS, ADAE, ADLBC, ADTTE integer(8) #> 4                        4 ADADAS, ADAE, ADLBC, ADTTE   text(32) #> 5                        4 ADADAS, ADAE, ADLBC, ADTTE integer(8) #> 6                        4 ADADAS, ADAE, ADLBC, ADTTE    text(1)

code: high_freq_vars <- extract_common_adsl_variables(   variable_info_df = variable_info,   min_domains_count = 3 ) head(high_freq_vars) #>   Variable SASFieldName DataType Length            Description  Origin #> 1      AGE          AGE  integer      8                    Age Derived #> 2   AGEGR1       AGEGR1     text      5     Pooled Age Group 1 Derived #> 3  AGEGR1N      AGEGR1N  integer      8 Pooled Age Group 1 (N) Derived #> 4     RACE         RACE     text     32                   Race Derived #> 5    RACEN        RACEN  integer      8               Race (N) Derived #> 6      SEX          SEX     text      1                    Sex Derived #>   CodelistOID DomainsCount               DomainsFound  SASLength #> 1                        4 ADADAS, ADAE, ADLBC, ADTTE integer(8) #> 2                        4 ADADAS, ADAE, ADLBC, ADTTE    text(5) #> 3                        4 ADADAS, ADAE, ADLBC, ADTTE integer(8) #> 4                        4 ADADAS, ADAE, ADLBC, ADTTE   text(32) #> 5                        4 ADADAS, ADAE, ADLBC, ADTTE integer(8) #> 6                        4 ADADAS, ADAE, ADLBC, ADTTE    text(1)

title: Extract Common ADSL Variables Across Analysis Domains — extract_common_adsl_variables
text: variable_info_df data.frame containing variable information extracted define.xml. Expected columns include: OID, Name, SASFieldName, DataType, Length, Description, Origin, CodelistOID, Dataset, others. adsl_dataset_name Character string specifying name subject-level dataset. Default "ADSL". include_sas_info Logical indicating whether include SAS-specific information output. Default TRUE. min_domains_count Integer specifying minimum number domains variable must appear included results. Default 1. sort_by Character string specifying sort results. Options "domains_count" (default), "variable_name", "data_type".

title: Extract Common ADSL Variables Across Analysis Domains — extract_common_adsl_variables
text: data.frame following columns: Variable Variable name ADSL SASFieldName SAS field name (include_sas_info = TRUE) DataType Data type (text, integer, float) Length Variable length specification Description Variable description define.xml Origin Variable origin (Predecessor, Derived, Assigned) CodelistOID Reference codelist applicable DomainsCount Number domains containing variable DomainsFound Comma-separated list domain names SASLength SAS length specification (include_sas_info = TRUE)

title: Extract Common ADSL Variables Across Analysis Domains — extract_common_adsl_variables
text: function performs following steps: Validates input parameters data structure Extracts variables specified ADSL dataset Identifies matching variables analysis domains Counts domain occurrences common variable Formats sorts results according specified criteria Common ADSL variables typically include: Study identifiers (STUDYID, USUBJID, SUBJID) Demographics (AGE, SEX, RACE, etc.) Treatment assignments (ARM, TRT01P, TRT01A, etc.) Study dates (TRTSDT, TRTEDT, etc.) Baseline characteristics

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Using the included define.xml file (recommended) define_path <- system.file("define.xml", package = "adrgOS") if (file.exists(define_path)) {   variable_info <- extract_variable_info_from_define(define_path)   common_vars <- extract_common_adsl_variables(variable_info)   print(common_vars)    # Filter by minimum domain count   high_freq_vars <- extract_common_adsl_variables(     variable_info,     min_domains_count = 3   )   print(high_freq_vars) }  # Alternative: Using custom sample data sample_data <- data.frame(   Name = c("STUDYID", "USUBJID", "AGE", "SEX", "STUDYID", "USUBJID", "AVAL",            "STUDYID", "USUBJID", "PARAMCD"),   Dataset = c("ADSL", "ADSL", "ADSL", "ADSL", "ADAE", "ADAE", "ADAE",               "ADLBC", "ADLBC", "ADLBC"),   DataType = c("text", "text", "integer", "text", "text", "text", "float",                "text", "text", "text"),   Length = c("12", "20", "3", "1", "12", "20", "8", "12", "20", "8"),   Description = c("Study Identifier", "Unique Subject ID", "Age", "Sex",                   "Study Identifier", "Unique Subject ID", "Analysis Value",                   "Study Identifier", "Unique Subject ID", "Parameter Code"),   Origin = c("Assigned", "Assigned", "Collected", "Collected",              "Assigned", "Assigned", "Derived", "Assigned", "Assigned", "Derived"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  # Basic usage result <- extract_common_adsl_variables(sample_data) print(result)  # Filter by minimum domain count (now works with improved sample data) result_filtered <- extract_common_adsl_variables(   sample_data,   min_domains_count = 2 ) print(result_filtered)  # Sort by variable name without SAS info result_sorted <- extract_common_adsl_variables(   sample_data,   include_sas_info = FALSE,   sort_by = "variable_name" ) print(result_sorted) } # }

what: List ADaM Programs, Packages, and Functions — list_adam_pgms
title: List ADaM Programs, Packages, and Functions — list_adam_pgms
text: function reads R ADaM programs list programs used packages/functions within . offers two output formats controlled adrg flag: nested list (data access) flattened data frame (documentation). automatically derives expected ADaM dataset name (.xpt) program file name.

title: List ADaM Programs, Packages, and Functions — list_adam_pgms
List ADaM Programs, Packages, and Functions — list_adam_pgms
text: target_dir file path program(s) processed.    all_one_file 'YN', directory path.    all_one_file 'NY', full path single R file.    Defaults current working directory (.). all_one_file flag controls processing scope:     'YN' (Default): Process ADaM files target_dir (matching ^ad.*\.[rR]$).       'NY': Process single file specified target_dir (matching ^ad.*\.[rR]$)..     adrg Flag select output format:     'Y' (Default): Returns Data Frame formatted Analysis Data Reviewers Guide (ADRG), package/function usage consolidated single string per program.       'N': Returns Nested List structure, program's package/function details stored nested data frame easy programmatic access.

title: List ADaM Programs, Packages, and Functions — list_adam_pgms
text: output format depends adrg flag:     adrg = 'Y' (Data Frame): Columns program, dataset, functions (single, newline-separated string).       adrg = 'N' (Nested List): list element :         program: R program file name.           dataset: derived ADaM dataset name.           packages_used: nested data frame columns package func_names.

title: List ADaM Programs, Packages, and Functions — list_adam_pgms
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # NOTE: These examples use non-portable file paths and require the files to exist.  # --- Scenario 1: Process ALL files, Output for ADRG (adrg='Y', default) --- # Returns a single data frame with collapsed functions per program. adrg_all_adams_df <- list_adam_pgms(   target_dir = "./dev/pilot3/m5/datasets/rconsortiumpilot3/analysis/adam/programs/",   all_one_file = 'YN',   adrg = 'Y' ) print(adrg_all_adams_df)  # --- Scenario 2: Process ALL files, Output as Nested List (adrg='N') --- # Returns a list where each program's details are nested. Ideal for programmatic access. all_adams_list <- list_adam_pgms(   target_dir = "./dev/pilot3/m5/datasets/rconsortiumpilot3/analysis/adam/programs/",   all_one_file = 'YN',   adrg = 'N' ) # Accessing the nested packages_used data frame for the first program: all_adams_list[[1]]$packages_used  # --- Scenario 3: Process ONE file, Output for ADRG (adrg='Y', default) --- # Returns a data frame with one row, formatted for the ADRG. adrg_one_adam_df <- list_adam_pgms(    target_dir = "./dev/pilot3/m5/datasets/rconsortiumpilot3/analysis/adam/programs/adlbc.r",    all_one_file = 'NY',    adrg = 'Y' ) print(adrg_one_adam_df)  # --- Scenario 4: Process ONE file, Output as Nested List (adrg='N') --- # Returns a list with one element (the specified program's details). one_adam_list <- list_adam_pgms(   target_dir = "./dev/pilot3/m5/datasets/rconsortiumpilot3/analysis/adam/programs/adlbc.r",   all_one_file = 'NY',   adrg = 'N' ) print(one_adam_list) } # }
